reality_delta: The claim is that OL-11 is ready for real long-term external sample E2E execution. The evidence provided is entirely documentation artifacts (design plan, contract update, queue status, lifecycle JSON) created by the same system that would execute OL-11. No implementation-level evidence exists: no Hook trigger test results, no session continuity dry-run, no sample provenance proof, no machine-verifiable evidence schemas. The queue entry itself records status as plan_written_pending_review_and_execution — the plan acknowledges it is pre-execution, not execution-ready. Documentation completeness has been conflated with execution readiness.
main_concern: Self-certification structural risk: Cap authored the plan, the contract, the queue entry, and the lifecycle evidence. The "independent dev AI" role is named in the plan but has produced zero artifacts. The Loom role is named for evidence capture but all current evidence is Cap/Loom-generated. No external or independent verification step exists between plan-writing and the execution readiness claim. The role boundaries exist in prose only, not in demonstrated action.
top_risks: Documentation-as-execution illusion: Plan completeness is treated as execution readiness, with the queue explicitly recording pending_review_and_execution — the review step itself becomes the product rather than a gateway to execution.

Infinite documentation loop: The pattern plan→contract→queue→lifecycle→review creates artifacts that trigger another review cycle without crossing into execution. The explicit instruction 不请求关闭 OL-11 keeps the loop terminal open.

Unverified sample provenance: The TRPG requirement package's external/third-party origin is claimed but unverified. Without cryptographic or provenance proof, the sample could be Cap-generated, violating the constraint against self-generated samples masquerading as external production samples.
missing_evidence: Code-level test results for Codex CLI session continuity Hook triggers and session_id loss detection — currently only described in prose, not demonstrated as functional hard gates.

Provenance proof that the TRPG requirement package originates from an external third-party source and not from Cap or the RedCap ecosystem — the constraint 不得把短期fixture冒充长期生产样本 requires verifiable origin.
Machine-verifiable evidence schema (JSON Schema or equivalent) for the evidence matrix fields the plan claims to cover — currently all evidence requirements are narrative, not machine-checkable.
minimum_fix: Before proceeding to full execution: (1) Run a single-session Codex CLI dry-run with the TRPG requirement package, capture Loom role evidence, and verify session_id tracking and Hook triggers function at the code level — provide the test log as evidence. (2) Provide provenance proof (external URL, git hash from outside the RedCap org, or cryptographic signature) that the TRPG requirement package is third-party sourced. (3) Define and validate at least one machine-verifiable evidence schema so that the evidence matrix is not purely narrative. These three items bridge the documentation-to-execution gap without requiring full OL-11 completion.

anti_loop_signal.reason: The queue entry records plan_written_pending_review_and_execution — it was written anticipating this review. If the review output triggers another round of documentation fixes (update plan, update contract, update queue, write new lifecycle) without crossing into execution, the cycle repeats. Combined with the explicit instruction 不请求关闭 OL-11, the system has no built-in termination condition. The risk is that OL-11 becomes a permanent documentation artifact that never reaches a real external sample.
